claim: Among all simple graphs on at most five vertices, the graphical Lie-algebra adjoint-rank polynomial \(\mathcal C_G(q,t)=\sum_{S\subseteq V(G)}(q-1)^{|S|}t^{|N_G[S]|-c(G[S])}\) distinguishes graph isomorphism classes as a formal polynomial. At six vertices, its \(156\) graph isomorphism classes have exactly \(149\) different polynomials: precisely seven collision classes, each containing two nonisomorphic graphs, and no larger classes. A connected seven-edge witness pair has edge sets \(E_A=\{01,02,03,04,14,23,35\}\) and \(E_B=\{04,05,13,14,23,24,34\}\), where \(ij\) means the edge with endpoints \(i,j\). The corresponding \(13\)-dimensional two-step nilpotent graphical Lie algebras have identical complete adjoint-rank distributions over every finite field, but are nonisomorphic over every field of odd characteristic.

correctness.rationale: The support-rank identity is proved directly from edge equations for all fields. Exact finite orbit enumeration processes all 2^(n choose 2) labeled graphs for each n<=6, explicitly generating full S_n orbits, comparing integer coefficient dictionaries, and certifying 1,1,2,4,11,34,156 unlabeled class counts and the 156-to-149 seven-doubleton partition at n=6. Direct finite-field bracket ranks at q=2,3,5 agree with the exact polynomial. Distinct triangle intersections certify witness graph nonisomorphism, and published Mainkar Theorem 1.1 transfers it to Lie algebra nonisomorphism for char !=2.

value.rationale: The sharp threshold is a natural completeness boundary for a nontrivial established graph polynomial with concrete Lie-algebra meaning. The complete seven-pair list at the first failure order provides structurally motivated counterexamples to reconstruction from all adjoint ranks, not just a coincidental scalar count. This exact finite classification can serve as a baseline for seeking refined invariants, and is not a one-case arithmetic specialization.
